cases.surface_condition: token before marker is a capitalized proper-name token (part of a multiword name) and token after the marker is a finite verb
cases.blamed_rule: Right begins with a finite verb or a new subject head (not a bound subordinator or preludial preposition), allowing the right to be translated independently.
cases.proposed_rule: If the immediate left token is capitalized (proper-name) and the immediate right token is a finite verb, treat this subject-NP ↔ predicate split as risky and lower the score to Middle (50–70).

cases.surface_condition: marker follows a short prepositional/directional phrase (preposition + short NP, ≤3 tokens) that carries a trailing comma, and the right begins a new subject+finite-verb clause
cases.blamed_rule: - Typical surface signals: left ends with a main verb + object/complements, or with a closing punctuation token attached to the previous word (e.g., a semicolon or comma that closes a parenthetic or subordinate clause), and the next token starts a new clause (a lexical head, a new subject, or a capitalized sentence-internal noun).
cases.proposed_rule: If the token immediately before the marker is the head of a short PP/adverbial (pattern: preposition + optional determiner + short noun/pronoun, ≤3 tokens) and it carries a trailing comma but does not contain a finite verb, lower the cut sharply to Low (0–20) because such short adjuncts almost always attach to the following clause.

cases.surface_condition: the token after the marker is a capitalized single-name (proper noun) and the token before the marker is a common-noun title or determiner+common-noun object (title + name pattern)
cases.blamed_rule: Right begins with a finite verb or a new subject head (not a bound subordinator or preludial preposition), allowing the right to be translated independently.
cases.proposed_rule: When the immediate right token is a capitalized single-token proper name and the immediate left token is a common-noun title or determiner+common-noun (e.g., 'Pharaoh', 'president', 'king'), demote the cut to Middle (40–60) because the right is likely an apposition or name that attaches to the left rather than an independent clause.

cases.surface_condition: the right begins with a restricting adverb ('only', 'just', case-insensitive) immediately followed by a preposition or numeral (e.g., 'only for five')
cases.blamed_rule: The remainder begins with a few words that could change polarity, participant identity, scope, or referent of the left (e.g., "but", "however", "rather", or a negation), or introduces a restricting relative clause that reinterprets the left head.
cases.proposed_rule: If the immediate right token is a restricting adverb like 'only' or 'just' followed by a preposition or numeral, push the cut into Low (0–10) because such sequences typically continue/limit the left and can reverse or reshape its meaning.

calibration_fix: Reserve 0–9 only for unmistakable fragments: shift the current 00–09 bucket upward (re-anchor those examples to ~20–29) so the lowest band reflects true unusable cuts rather than many moderately-good ones.
summary: The prompt systematically over-credits cuts where the right simply starts with a finite verb or a capitalized token (treating verb starts and trailing commas as automatic clause boundaries). It under-penalizes short adjuncts (short PPs/directional phrases with commas), restricting adverbial tails ('only ...'), and title+name appositions that attach rather than begin a new independent clause. Re-anchoring low-band calibration and adding surface tests for short adjuncts, restricting adverbials, and proper-name subject splits will reduce these high-contrast over-trust errors.
